title: Epithelial Dysmetabolism and Renal Fibrosis in ANCA Vasculitis
off: Epithelial Dysmetabolism and Renal Fibrosis in ANCA Vasculitis
collabs: Institut National de la Santé Et de la Recherche Médicale, France
summary: The project is to explore in humans the hypothesis of the link between the alteration of tubulo-interstitial metabolism and the rate of deterioration of renal function by comparing various nephropathies.
desc: Patients with ANCA vasculitis with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with "crescent" will be compared to six other groups made up of patients with another nephropathy 1/extramembranous glomerulonephritis and 2/ nephropathy with minimal glomerular lesion (LGM) characterized by the absence of significant tubulointerstitial fibrosis lesions and slow evolution towards end-stage chronic renal failure ). Other groups of patients will 3/have interstitial nephropathy, 4/IgA mesangial glomerulopathy , 5/diabetic nephropathy, or 6/collapsing focal segmental hyalinosis.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with an indication for initial diagnostic PBR on native kidney
* 18 ans ≥ Age ≤ 90 ans
* Affiliation to french health insurance
* Patient having given consent

For the ANCA vasculitis group:

• Diagnosis of ANCA vasculitis retained on renal biopsy with ANCA anti-proteinase 3 (PR3) or ANCA anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO)

For the control groups:

• Diagnosis retained after the renal biopsy

* Interstitial Nephritis
* Or glomerular nephropathy such as minimal change nephropathy
* Or Segmental hyalinosis in itscollapsing form
* Or Extramembranous Glomerulopathy,
* Or glomerulopathy with mesangial IgA deposits
* Or diabetic nephropathy.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Kidney transplant patient
* Patient on dialysis (hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis)
* Patient under legal protection, guardianship or curatorship
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Enrollement in an interventional study except studies relating to ANCA vasculitis and nephropathy with mesangial IgA deposits.
